- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- Model frequently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% bias to short-term forecasts if sentiment is mixed or trending.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from 0.33 to 0.67) triggers a 5–10% upward adjustment in forecast if model was underestimating; otherwise, wait 1–2 days before adjusting.
